title: Organizing Meals for a Neighbor After Surgery
script: Sari: [warmly] Tomo, did you hear that Pak Anwar had surgery last week? He lives alone, and I don't think anyone is checking on him.
Tomo: I didn't know that. Is he okay now? Surgery at his age sounds serious.
Sari: [thoughtful] He is home with discharge instructions, but I have not asked what support he wants or what food restrictions he has. His children live in another city.
Tomo: Let us first ask his permission and use one family contact. Then we can organize only the help he accepts.
Sari: [carefully] That's exactly why I called you. I want to organize the neighbors so we take turns bringing him dinner.
Tomo: I like that idea. How many houses were you thinking of asking?
Sari: [reflective] If he wants meals, perhaps eight families can cover agreed days and portions without overwhelming him.
Tomo: That sounds manageable for everyone. I can definitely take Tuesdays, since my wife already cooks extra on that day.
Sari: [gently] Perfect, I'll put you down for Tuesdays. I'm taking Mondays myself, right after I finish work.
Tomo: Should we create a group chat, so people don't accidentally bring food on the same evening?
Sari: [honestly] Yes, after consent. The chat will list tasks and allergies, not private operation details.
Tomo: What if he asks about medicine support?
Sari: [encouraging] We should not guess or discuss medicine in the group. He can follow his health team’s plan and choose whether a family contact helps.
Tomo: Good thinking. We should ask what he actually needs, instead of just guessing on our own.
Sari: [warmly] Exactly. I want this to genuinely help him, not just make us feel like good neighbors.
Tomo: It will help him. Honestly, just knowing people remembered him will probably matter as much as the food itself.
Sari: That's what I keep thinking too. Nobody should recover from surgery feeling forgotten by everyone around them.
Tomo: Send me that group chat link tonight. I'll message my sister too, since she lives two houses away from him.
Sari: Thank you, Tomo. I feel better already, knowing we're not leaving him to manage this alone.

quiz.question: What happened to Pak Anwar last week?
quiz.explanation: Sari explains that Pak Anwar had surgery last week.

quiz.question: Why can't Pak Anwar's children help him directly right now?
quiz.explanation: Sari says his children live in another city, so they can't check on him directly.

quiz.question: What plan does Sari propose to Tomo?
options: Organizing neighbors to take turns bringing him dinner
Asking him to cook for himself
quiz.explanation: Sari wants to organize the neighbors so they take turns bringing Pak Anwar dinner.

quiz.question: Why do they decide to create a group chat?
options: To sell things to each other
So people don't accidentally bring food on the same evening
quiz.explanation: They create a group chat so people don't accidentally bring food on the same day.

quiz.question: What does Tomo say will probably matter as much as the food?
quiz.explanation: Tomo says just knowing people remembered him will probably matter as much as the food itself.

quiz.question: What should Sari confirm before organizing meals?
options: Whether Pak Anwar wants help and what his discharge plan allows
Which neighbor cooks the most food
Whether his children will move home
quiz.explanation: Support begins with consent and actual instructions.

quiz.question: Why should the group ask about food restrictions?
options: Every older person eats the same diet
His recovery plan may limit certain foods
quiz.explanation: Suitable food depends on the person’s needs.

quiz.question: Who should answer medicine questions?
options: Pak Anwar and his health team, with an agreed family contact if he permits
quiz.explanation: Neighbors should not manage medicine by guessing.

quiz.question: What is the group chat for?
options: Coordinating agreed tasks without sharing private health details
quiz.explanation: Coordination should use minimum necessary information.

quiz.question: What does Tomo mean by not guessing?
options: Ask what help is wanted instead of assuming
Let one family cook every day
